zh.title: SyberJet聲稱SJ30-2創下美國輕型噴射機跨洲飛行速度紀錄
zh.summary: SyberJet表示SJ30-2橫越美國耗時4小時7分；尚待權威機構認證
body: 根據AeroTime報導，商務噴射機製造商SyberJet Aircraft於2026年8月21日表示，旗下SJ30-2噴射機創下美國由東向西的輕型噴射機跨洲飛行速度紀錄。該次飛行由飛行員Gordon Bryan執飛，自美國佛羅里達州傑克森維爾飛往加州聖地牙哥，耗時約4小時7分鐘，平均時速達505.3英里（約813.2公里）。
SyberJet指出，該項紀錄屬於國際航空聯合會（FAI）的C-1.f飛機類別，涵蓋重量在6000至9000公斤之間的動力陸上飛機。公司預計該紀錄在大約90天內獲得美國國家航空協會與FAI的正式認證。此外，SyberJet執行長Trevor Milton亦隨機飛行，公司目前正規劃於2032年取得新款九座噴射機SJ36的認證並投入營運。

en.title: SyberJet Claims Light Jet Transcontinental Speed Record with SJ30-2 Flight
en.summary: SyberJet claims an SJ30-2 light jet speed record after flying across the United States in four hours.
body: Executive aircraft manufacturer SyberJet Aircraft announced on August 21, 2026, that one of its SJ30-2 light jets set a new east-to-west transcontinental speed record in the United States. Flown by pilot Gordon Bryan, the aircraft traveled from Jacksonville, Florida, to San Diego, California, in approximately 4 hours and 7 minutes, achieving an average speed of 505.3 mph.

The company stated that the speed record falls under the FAI C-1.f aircraft category for powered landplanes weighing between 6,000 and 9,000 kg. SyberJet expects formal certification of the record from the National Aeronautic Association and the FAI within approximately 90 days. Chief Executive Officer Trevor Milton was also onboard the flight, as the manufacturer targets 2032 for the certification of its planned SJ36 light jet model.

SyberJet is targeting 2032 for certification and entry into service of this new aircraft type.

zh.title: 「藍天行動」實驗啟動 評估調整航路對凝結尾雲形成之影響
zh.summary: 「藍天行動」實驗已啟動；測試微調航班航路；評估減少凝結尾雲之暖化影響
body: 近期啟動的「藍天行動」（Operation Blue Skies）試驗項目，正在探索是否能透過對航班航路進行微幅調整，來減少具有氣候暖化效應的航機凝結尾雲形成。該項試驗使航空業的氣候影響課題再次受到關注。
當噴射發動機在高空燃燒燃料時，排放的水蒸氣與攝氏零下40度以下的嚴寒空氣混合，水蒸氣會凝結並凍結成冰晶，形成白色的凝結尾雲。航機巡航高度通常位於3萬至4萬英呎，該處的氣溫與濕度是決定是否產生凝結尾雲的關鍵因素。
若航機穿過冷濕且對冰飽和的空氣區域，凝結尾雲中的冰晶便能持續存在並擴散為卷雲，進而對氣候產生暖化作用。研究人員與航空公司正針對調整航路等預防措施展開調查與測試。

en.title: Operation Blue Skies Trial Tests Flight Path Alterations to Reduce Contrail Warming
en.summary: Operation Blue Skies trial launches; tests flight path tweaks; aims to reduce climate-warming contrail formation
body: The recently launched Operation Blue Skies trial is evaluating whether small adjustments to flight paths can reduce the formation of climate-warming contrails. The trial has renewed focus on aviation's broader atmospheric impacts beyond carbon dioxide emissions.

Contrails form when hot, moist exhaust from jet turbine engines mixes with freezing air at high cruising altitudes, typically between 30,000 and 40,000 feet, where temperatures can drop below minus 40 degrees Celsius. The resulting water vapour condenses and freezes into tiny ice crystals behind the aircraft.

When an aircraft travels through cold, ice-supersaturated air, these ice crystals can persist and spread into contrail cirrus clouds, creating a warming effect on the climate. Researchers and airlines are studying flight route adjustments to minimize contrail persistence.

facts.claim: Operation Blue Skies trial was launched to explore whether small flight path changes can reduce climate-warming contrails.
facts.sourceQuote: With the recent launch of Operation Blue Skies , a trial exploring whether small changes to flight paths can reduce the formation of climate-warming contrails, the issue has come under renewed scrutiny.

facts.claim: Contrails form when hot jet engine exhaust containing water vapour mixes with extremely cold high-altitude air and condenses into ice crystals.
facts.sourceQuote: When the hot, moist exhaust from an engine mixes with this freezing air, the water vapour can condense and freeze into tiny ice crystals.

facts.claim: In cold and sufficiently humid air, contrail ice crystals can persist and expand into contrail cirrus clouds with a climate warming effect.
facts.sourceQuote: If the air is cold and sufficiently humid with respect to ice, the ice crystals can survive and grow.

facts.claim: Cruising altitude temperature and humidity, usually between 30,000 and 40,000 feet, are key factors in contrail creation.
facts.sourceQuote: The type of aircraft, its engines and the route it flies also matter, but temperature and humidity at cruising altitude are particularly important.
